title: Polish a disk electrode in a figure-8, face flat
instruction: Polish the electrode's face on the alumina spot in figure-8 strokes, keeping the face flat on the pad with light pressure, then hang it in the stand's clamp with only its tip in the rinse water and let go.
context: Why: a glassy-carbon disk electrode is re-polished on alumina before most voltammetry runs, often daily, and robot chemistry platforms report this polishing as a manual step and a hurdle to automating electrochemistry. The maker's guide: keep the face parallel to the cloth, use a figure-8 while gently turning, about 3 mm of slurry, then suspend only the electrode surface in the rinse with a ring stand and clamp. The knack is contact control through a compliant arm: the face stays flat at light pressure while the hand sweeps two loops of opposite turn, and a tip held a few degrees off rides its edge and rounds the disk. Unlike grinding or filing down to a line, where firm pressure and the final shape count, here the load-cell force, the tilt and the path are what is scored. Then only the tip may go in the rinse: the shroud's upper part and stud stay dry. Done by: electrochemistry, battery and sensor researchers, lab technicians and students.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). (1) Load-cell platform: a 5 kg bar strain-gauge load cell under a 160 x 160 mm aluminium top, 4 cm tall, read at 80 Hz by an HX711 board logged to a laptop (about $20), centred at (25, 4); tared with the plate on it. (2) Taped to its top with double-sided tape: a 150 x 150 x 6 mm glass polishing plate covered by an adhesive-backed microcloth pad (Pine kit AKPOLISH); pad surface 4.7 cm above the table, wetted with DI water; a 3 mm round spot of 0.05 um alumina slurry (Pine kit) at the pad centre, (25, 4). (3) Rinse: a 100 mm wide, 50 mm tall borosilicate crystallizing dish with DI water 40 mm deep (water line 4.3 cm above the table), centred at (22, -16). (4) Ring stand: a 150 x 180 mm cast-iron base centred at (37.5, -16) and a 12 mm rod at (33, -16), with a spring-loaded burette clamp (e.g. United Scientific deluxe burette clamp: rubber-sleeved jaws held shut by springs) on a 6 mm arm 6 cm up: its jaws sprung shut to a 14 mm gap (1,500 N/m each: about 0.75 N on the shroud; measure the real clamp's grip), the round sleeves flaring the top, 20 mm long and 6 mm tall, 4.7-5.3 cm above the table over the dish centre; the tip is lowered into them from above and hangs where it is left. (5) Lint-free wipe folded to 60 x 60 x 1 mm at (13, -5). (6) The electrode: Pine E5-series disk electrode tip, glassy carbon, PTFE shroud (AFE5T050GC): a 5 mm glassy-carbon disk in a 15 mm PTFE shroud 25.4 mm long, 49 mm overall; above the shroud the stainless threaded stem, about 10 mm across (estimate); about 25 g (estimate; weigh it). Thin painted rings on the shroud 3 mm and 10 mm above the face. It starts standing face-down on the wipe. Cheaper option with the same body: the E5TQ ChangeDisk tip (PEEK) with a 5 mm glassy-carbon insert (AFED050P030GC). (7) Gripper pads wear nitrile covers (cut glove fingertips). (8) Cameras: two close-up side cameras at pad height, one looking along x and one along y, each with a printed 3-degree guide behind the pad. Friction 0.15 on the tip and pad, 0.6 on the clamp's rubber (estimates). Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged from the two side videos (calibrated with a ruler on the pad), the load-cell log (synced to the videos by a tap on the pad at the start) and a ruler. FORCE: the load-cell reading; light pressure is 1.0-5.0 N. A frame is IN BAND only if the force is 1.0-5.0 N and the face is the only thing touching the pad, plate or platform; any other contact (a finger, the other gripper, the shroud's side) makes the frame out of band. TILT: the shroud's axis from vertical on both side views; FLAT is 3 deg or less in both. TRACK: the face centre on the pad: its x from the camera looking along y and its y from the camera looking along x (the midpoint of the shroud's silhouette 5 mm above the face, below the grip, so no hand hides it and turning does not change it). CROSSING CIRCLE: 10 mm radius round the slurry spot. LOBE: the track from one exit of the crossing circle to its next entry. It counts only if it reaches 20 mm or more from the spot, its loop is 10 mm or more wide square to the line from the spot to its farthest point, at least 90% of its frames are in band and flat, none above 6 deg or 8 N, and no finger goes below the 10 mm ring. Its TURN: clockwise or anticlockwise seen from above. DIVIDING LINE: through the spot, square to the line from the spot to the farthest point of all lobes. FIGURE-8S: the longest run of consecutive lobes alternating sides of the dividing line and turning opposite ways, divided by 2 (10 lobes = 5 figure-8s, about 30 s; the guide gives no count). Gently turning the tip, as the guide suggests, is allowed and not scored. RINSED: after the last lobe and no pad contact after it, the face 3-10 mm below the water line (between the 3 mm and 10 mm rings) for 2 s or more. If the 10 mm ring goes under water at any time, the rinse fails for the rest of the run. HUNG: rinsed and held only by the clamp, face 3-10 mm under, both grippers 2 cm or more away, moving under 1 mm over the last 1 s. Ladder, first row that fits at the end: 1.0: 5 or more figure-8s and HUNG; 0.75: 5 or more figure-8s and rinsed; 0.5: 5 or more figure-8s; 0.25: 2 or more lobes in any pattern; 0: anything else, including straight strokes and the untouched start. Sticky 0 at any time, even if put back: the tip drops (falls 20 mm or more held by nothing), or its face comes within 1.5 mm of the bench outside the wipe or of the dish floor. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit or after 1.0 holds 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the tip out of the clamp and wipe its face, re-dot 3 mm of 0.05 um alumina at the pad centre and re-wet the pad, top the dish to 40 mm with DI water, stand the tip face-down on a fresh folded wipe, tare the load cell. The pad wears: move to a fresh area or change it as the maker's guide says. Nothing else is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Alumina, water and wear are not simulated: the slurry spot is a painted mark and the rinse is the face's depth under a fixed water line (non-colliding water). The load cell is a stiff 10,000 N/m spring under the plate (0.5 mm at 5 N); its deflection gives the force. The tip collides as 15 mm and 9 mm square prisms (drawn round); the clamp's jaws slide on 1,500 N/m springs. Friction, the 25 g mass and the 10 mm stem are estimates to measure.
